QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_36

question.text: In SIA fieldwork, Section 5.11.4 distinguishes between probabilistic and non-probabilistic sampling methods. Which of the following correctly pairs a method with its category?

answer.text: Stratified sampling — probabilistic; Quota sampling — non-probabilistic
All sampling methods in SIA are non-probabilistic

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.8 'Primary Data' sub-section and Section 5.11.4 state: 'a combination of probabilistic sampling methods (simple random / systematic / cluster / stratified) or non-probabilistic methods (quota, judgemental, snowball) can be used to collect evidence.' So stratified is probabilistic and quota is non-probabilistic — Option C is correct. The Trap: A mis-classifies simple random; B mis-classifies snowball; D overstates that all methods are non-probabilistic. Cross-Exam Context: Sampling taxonomy in NISM XV (RA) and research-methods literature aligns with XXIII's split. Assessor's Pro-Tip: For SAS 1600 (migrant welfare) or SAS 400 (LGBTQIA+) engagements where beneficiary frames are incomplete, snowball sampling is often the only feasible route — disclose the trade-off (non-probabilistic, wider CI) clearly in the AIR methodology section.
